US.why: Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75% but 3 dissents wanted a HIKE; Sep-16 FOMC is live. Payrolls -23k, unemployment 4.1%. Core CPI 2.5% contained, headline 3.4% and rising on Brent. NDX 22.4x fwd is BELOW its 10y (22.9x) and 5y (24.7x) averages. IMF: 2.4% growth 2026.

EUROPE.why: Worst policy/growth mismatch in the world: ECB HIKED +25bp to 2.25% in June - first hike in 3 years - into IMF growth of just 0.7% for 2026 (down from 1.1%). Largest net energy importer facing Brent +32% y/y. Offset: cheapest large market at 15.4x fwd, +9.5% YTD.

ASIA.why: Best fundamentals available: 10.5x fwd P/E with consensus EPS growth of ~52% (2026) and ~28% (2027) off the AI/memory/semis cycle. Korea +71% and Taiwan +49% YTD means momentum is real but crowded. JPM LTCMA puts EM equity at 7.8% - the highest of any equity block.

PHILIPPINES.why: Cash is genuinely paid here. BSP hiked +25bp to 4.75%; T-bills at 5.14% (91d) to 5.72% (364d) against ~4% inflation = positive real carry with zero duration risk. Fades over 5y as BSP normalises.

drivers.name: Monetary policy & liquidity
drivers.note: Global tightening BIAS, not easing: Fed 9-3 hold with 3 hike dissents, ECB +25bp (first in 3y), BSP +25bp. Three of three relevant central banks leaning hawkish at once.

drivers.name: Inflation trajectory
drivers.note: US core 2.5% is fine; US headline 3.4% and re-accelerating on energy. Euro HICP 3.0% for 2026. PH above the 4% ceiling in both 2026 and 2027.

drivers.name: Growth momentum
drivers.note: IMF: global 3.1% (2026) / 3.2% (2027). US resilient at 2.4%. Euro area cut to 0.7%. Wide dispersion - a stock-picker's macro, not a beta macro.

drivers.name: Corporate earnings
drivers.note: The single strongest pillar. Asia ex-Japan EPS ~+52% (2026) / ~+28% (2027); AI infrastructure capex still compounding through the semis supply chain.

drivers.name: Valuation support
drivers.note: NDX 22.4x fwd sits BELOW both its 10y and 5y averages. Asia at 10.5x is a two-decade-wide discount. Europe 15.4x. No broad bubble multiple.

drivers.name: Volatility & risk appetite
drivers.note: Textbook complacency: VIX printed a 2026 low of 14.13 while the futures curve is in steep contango (Sep 17.92, Dec 20.38). The market is cheaply priced for calm it does not expect to keep.

drivers.name: Geopolitics & energy
drivers.note: The clear weak link. Active US/Israel-Iran hostilities, naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Brent $91.28 (+32% y/y) after a Q1 spike to $118.

corr_note: Money market is treated as uncorrelated to the equity sleeves. Nasdaq Equity Income / Global Technology at 0.88 is the binding constraint - both are US mega-cap-tech engines, so holding both at size buys far less diversification than it appears to.

scenarios.name: Hormuz escalation
scenarios.desc: Strait of Hormuz closure; Brent to $130+. Global CPI re-accelerates, Fed forced to hike, multiples compress hardest at the long end.

scenarios.name: Hawkish repricing
scenarios.desc: The 3 July dissents win; Fed hikes into a 4.1% unemployment rate. Duration-heavy growth de-rates.

scenarios.name: AI capex digestion
scenarios.desc: Semis order book rolls over; the 52% Asia EPS estimate is cut. Hits the AI supply chain and mega-cap tech together.

scenarios.name: Disinflation restart
scenarios.desc: Oil mean-reverts to $65, headline CPI falls to 2%, Fed cuts. The bull case: multiples expand, vol collapses.

scenarios.name: Grind-on base case
scenarios.desc: Vol drifts up to the 19-20 the futures curve already prices, earnings hold, no policy accident. The modelled path.
